newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 80 die as faction fighting escalates in Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: 80 die as faction fighting escalates in Mogadishu.

text.p: More than 80 people died and at least 150 were wounded in 24 hours of weekend fighting in south Mogadishu between rival factions, witnesses reported.

The fighting, between the forces of warlord Hussein Mohamed Aideed and those of rival factions leaders Osman Hassan Ali Atto and Musa Sidi Yalahow, began on Saturday in the Medina district and continued on Sunday.

Local residents said the violence began when Aideed's men entered the main market and began looting market stalls, petrol stations and houses. Several taxis were driven off by Aideed's men before the other armed groups arrived and drove them back.
The anti-Aideed group used heavily armed technicals -- makeshift armoured vehicles -- anti-aircraft missiles and mortars. Stray mortar rounds damaged houses in surrounding residential areas.
Panic spread on Sunday when mortar shells landed in the heavily-populated area around the market, killing 20 women, according to witnesses.
Among the civilian casualties was a family of nine, where only the father survived, residents said.
Sporadic gunfire continued after the main group of Aideed's men was driven back, and witnesses said both sides were trying to gain more territory.
Scared residents fled the area, and efforts by clan elders to halt the fighting were to no avail.
A senior officer in the Aideed faction was quoted as telling his men that this was only the beginning of the war.

Ali Mahdi Mohamed, whose forces control north Mogadishu, ordered the reinforcement of his armed guards along the "green line" separating north and south Mogadishu, raising fears that they might join in the fighting if it continued.
